format: one multifunction Core ML package; ship the compiled eye.mlmodelc (Core ML caches the Neural Engine program by its path)

photo.input: image: float16 RGB in 0..1, (1, 3, H, W); normalisation is inside the model, 384x384 centre crop (resize the short side to 384, bicubic)

photo_peak.note: photo plus the peak-moment branch; use for burst / video frames

spatial.input: image: float16 RGB in 0..1, (1, 3, H, W); normalisation is inside the model, whole frame squashed to 384x384 (bicubic)
spatial.note: run only when a crop, boxes or shot type are requested

faces_detect.input: image: float16 RGB in 0..1, (1, 3, H, W); normalisation is inside the model, 768x768, photo scaled so its long side is 768, pasted top-left on grey (114)

faces_analyze.input: image: float16 RGB in 0..1, (1, 3, H, W); normalisation is inside the model, 128x128 square crop 1.4x the face box

sharp_4x3.input: image: float16 gray in 0..1, (1, 1, 576, 768); pick the aspect closest to the photo

sharp_3x4.input: image: float16 gray in 0..1, (1, 1, 768, 576); pick the aspect closest to the photo

sharp_16x9.input: image: float16 gray in 0..1, (1, 1, 432, 768); pick the aspect closest to the photo

sharp_9x16.input: image: float16 gray in 0..1, (1, 1, 768, 432); pick the aspect closest to the photo

outputs.focus: logits [none, defocus, motion] then bokeh score
outputs.pet_attrs: logits [quality, face_visible, facing_camera, eyes_open, sharp, cut_off, occluded]
outputs.peak_logits: [airborne, peak, action, dramatic]; peak score = logit 1
outputs.subject: 64x64 logits of where people look (softmax over all cells)
outputs.detections: pet / person heatmap, size, offset at 48x48: decode as ml_eye.stages.train_pet_det decode, then detection_postprocess

compression: PE-Core weights 6-bit k-means palettes per 16 output channels, palette values calibrated by distillation (ml_eye.stages.qat --lut-only); 3 sensitive weights 8-bit palettes; heads and face / sharpness models int8; lookup tables fp16

litert.format: one LiteRT model, a signature per function, named as the Core ML functions (input `image`, outputs by name); XNNPACK on CPU, or a GPU delegate (every op is GPU-supported)
litert.input: float32 instead of float16; shapes, layout (1, C, H, W), range 0..1 and preparation as for Core ML
litert.compression: weights int8 per output channel, dequantized at load (activations float32); the sharpness model float32; PE-Core from its float weights
